About

Free online pool, snooker and three-cushion billiards

Tailuge Billiards is a free, open-source billiards, pool and snooker simulator that runs in any modern desktop or mobile browser — nothing to install, no account to create. Play, practise, analyse shots or explore how billiards physics works. The table is drawn in 3D with WebGL and three.js on a physics engine built from published work on ball motion, collisions and cushion impacts.

What you can play

  • Nine-ball — the fast rotation game, with a build-a-layout practice mode and shareable replay links.
  • 8-ball — solids and stripes, with a Hi-Res rendering mode.
  • Snooker — full-size 12-foot tables with 15 reds, plus shorter games on a 6-foot table.
  • Three-cushion carom — the discipline the cushion model is tuned hardest against, with a beginner mode.
  • Sagu — the Korean four-ball carom game, also playable on a small 5-foot table.

Two practice bots, ClawBreak and TheFarJaw, play when nobody else is around; the speedrun challenge races you against the clock, and the reveal game uncovers pictures with straight-pool potting.

Realistic billiards physics

The engine is deliberately lightweight and deterministic; each effect a player notices follows a specific published model rather than being tuned by feel. Ball motion follows Han (2005) with corrections noted by Kiefl; ball-to-ball collisions follow Alciatore, including the throw effect; and cushion impacts use Mathavan (2010), with Stronge's compliant-cushion model available as an alternative. Spin, throw and cushion rebound can all be inspected and re-tuned on the three-cushion physics page.

Practise and measure your game

  • Practice table — set up any shot or position and repeat it, with no opponent and no clock.
  • Billiards exam — a graded shot list with a front sheet that reports an assessment level, completion and score.
  • Snooker exam — the same course on a snooker table, from basic pots to awkward positions.
  • Three-cushion exam — the shot list for carom, graded from basic to advanced.
  • Shot sensitivity analysis — see how aim, spin, power and elevation change the result.
  • The diamond system for three-cushion cue-ball paths.

Play against other people

The lobby lists who is online so you can challenge someone directly, there is a two-tab mode for playing across two windows on one machine, and hourly arenas run lichess-style half-hour tournaments. Highest breaks go to a leaderboard and rated games feed a Glicko2 ELO rating.

Guides and write-ups

  • Why most pool games feel wrong — what makes a physics engine read as real, and where the cheap ones cheat.
  • Clearing the line-up — a practice log on running the balls, and how to drill it on the practice table.
  • Implementing Mathavan cushion physics — the maths behind the cushion model, written up in the open.

Open source

Plain TypeScript with three.js for rendering, open source under the GNU GPL. The code is on GitHub, and contributions — bugs, physics tweaks, translations, new rule sets — are welcome. Read more on the about page.
